title: Surgical prefetch debloat and KV atomicity migration
creator: Ava Chen
description: We have observed sustained memory and CPU overhead from an overly-general prefetch state machine and conservative KV cache locking in the continuous batching path. This ticket surgically removes redundant prefetch code paths, replaces heavyweight lock sequences with an atomic swap-based reconciliation for KV metadata, and upgrades a small set of runtime dependencies to unlock lock-free primitives. Goal: reduce tail latency for short requests, decrease CPU and allocation pressure during surges, and simplify the prefetch contract so future follow-ups can be smaller and lower risk.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile tail latency for requests <512 tokens drops by at least 20% in the lab workload (p50/p95/p99 baseline provided)
KV cache CPU overhead reduced (allocs/sec down by >= 15% for steady-state QPS), validated by perf counters and flamegraphs
New prefetch state machine replaces legacy branchy codepaths and has unit and integration tests covering eviction races and restart behavior
Dependency upgrades applied with compatibility tests green (tokio/bytes/byteorder crates), and the change is documented in the runtime upgrade notes
No increase in error rate or user-visible 5xxs in the canary region for 72h post rollout
comments: 2025-11-14 - Ava Chen: Kickoff — scoped this to three surgical changes: 1) collapse duplicate prefetch queues, 2) implement atomic metadata swap for kvcache markers, 3) bump tokio/bytes to get access to updated atomic-friendly APIs. Lowered blast radius by avoiding a full state-machine rewrite.
